gaps.sentence: What ___ in the garage? I can hear drilling.
gaps.hint: can hear shows evidence happening now
gaps.explanation: The present evidence of noise shows something in progress now, so the present continuous fits: is going on.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ across the desert.
gaps.hint: action in progress at a future time
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' — future continuous for an ongoing future action.

gaps.sentence: I ___ from Tom since March, which is starting to worry me.
gaps.hint: since March continuing into the present
gaps.explanation: 'Since March' up to now takes the present perfect: haven't heard.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: Every time I visit, she ___ something delicious from the garden.
gaps.hint: every time marks a repeated habit
gaps.explanation: 'Every time' marks a repeated action, which takes the present simple: brings.

gaps.sentence: I ___ you were coming today — nobody told me!
gaps.hint: state verb forbids the past continuous
gaps.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb, so its past form is the past simple: didn't know.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.
